subject.title: Per-agent compaction and contextPruning overrides in agents.list

question: Should OpenClaw support `agents.list[].compaction` and `agents.list[].contextPruning` as a public per-agent config contract, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88506 be the landing path?
rationale: The source-reproduced gap is real, but adding this surface changes public configuration, context-retention behavior, and provider/auth-profile routing semantics.

options.title: Sponsor the additive contract
options.body: Approve per-agent compaction and context-pruning overrides, require deep-merge semantics plus docs/tests/upgrade proof, and use the open PR as the repair or replacement path.

options.title: Narrow to compaction model first
options.body: Accept only `agents.list[].compaction.model` now and defer broader compaction/context-pruning knobs to a later design issue.

options.title: Keep defaults-only behavior
options.body: Decline this config expansion and close or redirect the open implementation PRs, leaving users with global defaults or separate deployments.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the additive contract
recommendation.body: Approve per-agent compaction and context-pruning overrides, require deep-merge semantics plus docs/tests/upgrade proof, and use the open PR as the repair or replacement path.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has recent history on the config schema and agent-scope resolver paths where the contract would land.
